name: Easy chicken gyoza with lace crust (גיוזה Easy Mode — בצל ירוק ועירית)

source.author: Instagram (Hebrew caption)
source.notes: Shortcut gyoza using ready-rolled chilled dumpling wrappers (Shimrit brand, from the fridge section — no thawing, no rolling, simple top-pinch fold with sides left open). Minced chicken + soy + miso + garlic + ginger + sesame oil + spring onion + chives filling, pan-fried then steamed with a flour-water-oil 'lace' (crispy skirt). Makes ~20; analyzed as 4 servings of ~5 gyoza. Posted as the spicy version — chili crunch in the filling and dip is optional and included here (drop it to save ~170 kcal / ~17 g fat across the batch). Wrapper weight assumed ~8 g each. Dipping sauce counted at ~50% consumed. Chicken breast mince assumed (thigh/pargit mince adds fat). Estimate.

steps: Wet the wrapper edges, add ~1 tbsp filling and pinch closed across the top, leaving the sides open.
Whisk the lace mixture (water, flour, oil).
Fry the gyoza in a lightly oiled nonstick pan over medium until the bottoms are golden; stir the lace mix and pour in just enough to cover the pan base.
Cover ~1 min to steam, then uncover and let the water evaporate until the lace dries and crisps. Lower the heat if the bottoms brown too fast.

batch_totals.note: ~20 gyoza + ~half the dip. Fat comes mostly from sesame oil, the lace oil and the optional chili crunch (filling + dip); sodium from soy (filling + dip) and miso.

him.verdict: Good, fun protein option — ~22.7 g protein per 5 gyoza for ~341 kcal (~6.7 g protein per 100 kcal) with lean chicken-breast filling. What holds it back: the oils stack (sesame oil, lace oil, and optional chili crunch in both filling and dip), the wrappers are refined carbs with little fibre, and soy in both filling and dip pushes sodium up. Skip the chili crunch and go easy on the dip and it climbs to ~8.
flags: fat ~14.7 g/serving — sesame oil + lace oil + chili crunch
sodium ~934 mg/serving — soy in filling + dip, plus miso
suggested_mods: Skip the chili crunch in the filling (keep a little in the dip if you want heat) — saves the most fat
Use low-sodium soy in both filling and dip, and dip lightly
Halve the lace oil — a nonstick pan still gives a crisp skirt
Serve with a big side of steamed greens / edamame for fibre

her_preconception.verdict: Solid lean protein, fully cooked (minced chicken must be cooked through — steam step handles it), no safety flags. Not a folate/iron/DHA source on its own and fairly salty; pair with a vegetable side.

safety_advisories.note: Minced chicken must be cooked through — check a gyoza is firm/opaque inside after steaming.
safety_advisories.swap: steam a little longer if unsure

suggested_mods: Low-sodium soy; serve with greens or edamame for folate

cooking_guide: Keep the filling cold and mix it well — it binds better and is easier to spoon.
Only ~1 tbsp filling per wrapper; overfilling stops the top seal from holding.
Wet just the edges, not the whole wrapper, so it seals without going gummy.
Brown the bottoms first on medium, then add the lace — the order is what gives a crisp base plus a steamed top.
Re-stir the lace mix right before pouring (the flour sinks), and pour only a thin layer across the pan base.
After ~1 min covered, uncover and let it fry until the skirt is dry, golden and releases easily — flip onto a plate in one piece.
